open_points.subject: perform_recovery_override eligibility
open_points.text: “The administrative recovery override (R0-20) is the one operation that replaces a login email; it is an exceptional flow” and “a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Beyond administrator authorization and ordinary email validity/uniqueness, what condition makes an email replacement an eligible recovery override, and which calls must be refused as non-exceptional ordinary email changes?
options: Any authorized administrator may invoke it whenever the replacement email is valid and unique.
It is allowed only when a defined recovery condition or evidence exists.
It is allowed only for accounts in specified statuses or access-loss states.
open_points.default_guess: Allow any authorized administrator when the normalized replacement email is valid and unique, because no recovery-condition state or evidence is modeled.

witness.initial: Administrator A and active staff account S exist; S has login email old@example.com, and there is no recorded indication that S lost access.
events: A invokes perform_recovery_override for S with new@example.com.
outcomes: The operation succeeds because recovery_override is the sole administrator-authorized email replacement operation.
The operation is refused because no exceptional recovery condition has been established.
witness.observer: A sees success versus refusal; S can log in only with a different email in the success outcome.

open_points.subject: IAM invariant range
open_points.text: The row declares “INV-001…INV-015” while the same row says “INV-010…INV-013 and INV-016, the email challenges, removed,” and the Status also says INV-011 was removed.
open_points.question: What is the exact surviving IAM invariant ID set: does the literal range still include INV-010 through INV-013, or must later closures treat those IDs as nonexistent?
options: The surviving set is INV-001–INV-009 plus INV-014–INV-015; all challenge IDs are absent.
INV-001–INV-015 remains a complete required range despite the removal note.
The row is a historical area range whose holes must be represented explicitly elsewhere.
open_points.default_guess: Treat INV-001–INV-009 and INV-014–INV-015 as the surviving set and omit INV-010–INV-013 and INV-016.

open_points.subject: security-review model scope
open_points.text: “authentication_credential_abuse: APPLICABLE; references: A3, A4, A10, A11, A16, A17, A25; affected: M01-M15”
open_points.question: After M08–M12 were removed, does this security category cover only the surviving identity models M01–M07 and M13–M15, or are later agents expected to retain some security obligation corresponding to the removed models?
options: Replace the range with the surviving models M01–M07 and M13–M15.
Keep M01–M15 as a historical range but ignore missing model numbers.
Retain separate security requirements for the removed challenge and email-delivery concepts.
open_points.default_guess: Scope the category to M01–M07 and M13–M15 only.
